notes: Harker Experi(Mental): 18 teams, guillotine, and the only league with IDP. The 2025 draft cleared its defensive players between rounds 7 and 11, peaking at 8-11, which is what these deadlines are built around. Caveat: only 42% of that draft's Yahoo player ids resolved to positions, and defensive players are the ones most likely to be missing, so the real IDP concentration may start earlier than it looks.

rules.label: RB-RB start
rules.note: Eighteen teams means replacement level is brutal everywhere. Anchor the backfield first.

rules.label: Two linebackers by round 10
rules.note: Linebackers are the deepest and best-paying IDP group in this scoring — two points a solo tackle, one an assist — and they cleared earliest in 2025. The deadline used to say round sixteen, written for a season that wanted two defensive starters per team. This one wants seven, a hundred and twenty-six across the league and a third of every pick, so the pool empties far sooner than the old number allowed for.

rules.label: Two defensive linemen by round 11
rules.note: Sacks pay six, so the top edge rushers carry real weekly upside and go a round or so after the linebackers. Eighty-two per cent of all IDP was gone by round eleven in 2025, with a third of this year's demand.

rules.label: Two defensive backs by round 12
rules.note: The flattest of the three groups — safeties who play every snap are close to interchangeable — so this is the one to leave latest, but not past the point where the position is picked over.

rules.label: QB after the top two
rules.note: Not paying up for Josh Allen or Lamar Jackson.

rules.label: No one who will not play
rules.note: Elimination is weekly, so a pick that does not play in September may never play for you at all. Anyone carrying a real absence is kept off the board here. Questionable is not: fifty-nine ranked players carry it in August, McCaffrey and Chase among them, and acting on it would delete the top of the board — it is shown and left to you.

rules.label: Kicker last
rules.note: No team defence in this league — the D slot takes a defensive player, not a unit — so the kicker is the only mandatory pick left at the end.

note: No late-target rule here, unlike the other three leagues. Rookies and handcuffs are season-long bets, and this league eliminates the lowest scorer every week — a handcuff pays off in a week you may not reach, and the pool of eliminated teams' players hits waivers anyway, so bench depth is cheaper to buy later than to draft. Every pick has to score from week one. The D slot takes a seventh defensive player from any of the three groups; no deadline covers it, because a flex fills from whichever group is still worth taking and a rule naming one would be guessing.
